paragraphs.text: A [Liu An basket tea](liu-an:definition) from Anhui, made in 1990. Despite the name, the style belongs to Qimen County in the south of the province, not to the city of Lu'an. It is a [dark tea](dark:definition), not the green [Lu'an Guapian](anhui:lu-an-names) that shares part of its name. Its making explains why it is kept: after firing over charcoal, the leaf is spread outdoors for one night to take the [night dew](liu-an:making). It is then steamed, packed into baskets lined with bamboo leaf and fired again, and it is sold only after resting for some years.

The year matters. Basket tea was made for the [southern trade](liu-an:southern-trade) to Guangdong, Hong Kong, Macau and Southeast Asia. Production stopped in the 1930s and 1940s, when war cut that trade off. In 1983 tea people from Hong Kong sent an aged basket to Anhui and asked for it to be made again, and commercial making returned in the early 1990s. A tea from 1990 comes from the very start of that revival.

At thirty-six years it has rested far longer than the style asks. Liu An is [said to improve with years](liu-an:ageing) if it is kept dry, clean and away from smells, in wrapping that breathes, so its storage has shaped it as much as its age.

brewing.text: Use water at or near the boil, rinse the leaf quickly, and keep the steeps short, each a little longer than the last, in a gaiwan or clay pot; doses run from about 3 to 8 grams for 100 ml, for six to ten or more steeps. A small piece of the basket's bamboo leaf is often brewed with it. Aged tea can also be simmered in a larger pot, about 1 gram to 200 to 300 ml, for a few minutes or longer.

notice.text: A redder, browner liquor, the smoke gone, and the cup moving toward medicinal, woody and camphor notes, often with betel nut.

unsupported.sentence: Its making explains why it is kept: after firing over charcoal, the leaf is spread outdoors for one night to take the night dew.
unsupported.words: Its making explains why it is kept
unsupported.why: No claim links the dew step, or any making step, to the reason the tea is kept. The making claim only describes the steps and says the tea rests for some years before sale.

unsupported.sentence: A tea from 1990 comes from the very start of that revival.
unsupported.words: comes from the very start of that revival
unsupported.why: The claim says only that commercial making returned in the early 1990s, with no exact start year. Nothing supports placing a 1990 tea at the very start of the revival or tying this lot to it.

unsupported.sentence: Liu An is said to improve with years if it is kept dry, clean and away from smells, in wrapping that breathes, so its storage has shaped it as much as its age.
unsupported.words: so its storage has shaped it as much as its age
unsupported.why: No claim says storage matters as much as age, and nothing records how this lot was stored. The ageing claim also does not make the improvement depend on those storage conditions; it lists them as separate advice.
